myGov, Centrelink, Medicare and the ATO after a death (Australia)

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 19 Oct 2026

Tell Services Australia within 28 days by phone, with the Advice of death form (SA116) or at a service centre; it uses the form to update Medicare, Centrelink and Child Support records. You don't need to close the person's myGov account, because myGov closes unused accounts. Notify the ATO separately with a death certificate or grant of probate.

Key facts

  • Services Australia: tell it within 28 days
  • SA116 updates Medicare, Centrelink and Child Support records
  • myGov: no need to close; unused accounts close automatically
  • ATO: up to 28 days to update records after notification

What are the steps?

  1. Get the death certificate from your state or territory's Births, Deaths and Marriages registry. A funeral director may register the death for you.
  2. Within 28 days, tell Services Australia: call, send the Advice of death form (SA116a for an adult, SA116b for a child), or visit a service centre. Services Australia uses the form to update Medicare, Centrelink and Child Support records.
  3. Don't sign in to their myGov. The myGov terms of use say you're not allowed to access another person's myGov account, and myGov says you don't need to close it.
  4. If you don't have documents yet, phone the ATO to say the person has died. It will pause their tax correspondence.
  5. Officially notify the ATO with its Notification of a deceased person form: online, followed by an interview at a participating Australia Post outlet, or on paper with certified copies.
  6. Executors who plan to apply for probate or letters of administration: the ATO suggests waiting for the grant before notifying it, to avoid delays. With a grant, it records you as the authorised legal personal representative (LPR).
  7. To get the person's details from Services Australia for the estate, each executor or administrator completes an Executor/Administrator Request for information form and gives proof of authority.
  8. Check whether you can get a bereavement payment or other support from Services Australia.
  9. Use the free Australian Death Notification Service to tell participating organisations at once (Telstra and Vodafone, for example, accept it).

Frequently asked questions

Do I need to close a deceased person's myGov account?

No. myGov says you don't need to close it because it closes automatically after not being used. Its terms say accounts may be closed after 24 months without a sign-in, or 6 months if no services are linked.

How long do I have to tell Services Australia about a death?

Services Australia asks to be told within 28 days. You can call, send the Advice of death form (SA116) or visit a service centre.

Can I log in to my late parent's myGov?

No. The myGov terms of use say you're not allowed to access another person's myGov account. Use the official notification forms instead.

What do I need to notify the ATO of a death?

One of: a death certificate, a grant of probate or letters of administration, or a certified copy of the will (only if you're not applying for a grant). The ATO says it takes up to 28 days to update the person's records.

Who can get the deceased's tax and super information from the ATO?

The authorised legal personal representative. Without a grant of probate or letters of administration, the ATO can't record you as the authorised LPR, which limits what it can release.

Do I tell the ATO and Services Australia separately?

Yes. myGov's checklist lists them as separate agencies to tell. The free Australian Death Notification Service can tell participating private organisations at once.
